Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork as dated entries with assigned identifiers, routing each document through a defined sequence of verification checks and sign-off fields before final disposition in the case register.
2) What occurred:
- On a dated entry, the actor duplicated a ticket document field into several separate records; the unique serialization check on the document field remained unverified.
- On a dated entry, the actor altered the buyer assignment field on the first copied record to precede gate processing; the queue order sign-off on that field remained unverified.
- On a dated entry, the actor set the refund status field to a suppressed state across the copied records; the reconciliation check on the refund status field remained unverified.
- On a dated entry, the actor set the chargeback flag field to a disabled state on the copied records; the transaction review sign-off on that field remained unverified.
- On a dated entry, the actor set the identification verification field to a pending state on the copied records; the identity confirmation check on that field remained unverified.
3) Materials/access observed: The actor used a single source ticket document with an identifier field, a named account linked to a dated record, and the electronic channel through which the duplicated records were transmitted to a second named account.
4) Indicators & artifacts: Multiple records sharing the same serialization field value; a queue order field preceding the original document's order; a refund status field in a suppressed state on records lacking reconciliation; a chargeback flag field disabled without transaction review; an identification verification field pending without confirmation.
